title: The kernel of the finite coefficient projection is uniformizer-power divisible
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell with integer ring O and chosen uniformizer pi [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme T with its small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site]. Let B be the inverse limit of the positive uniformizer-power constant quotient ring sheaves, and c:O_T -> B its constant-scalar map [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients; def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every n >= 0, every site object U and section x of B over U, if its projection to (O/(pi)^(n+1))_T over U is zero, then there exists a section y of B over U such that x=c(pi)^(n+1)y.

proof.text:
Put O = O_E and pi = pi_E. The recorded DVR structure makes pi a nonzero
nonzerodivisor. For every r >= 1, multiplication by pi^(n+1) induces an additive
isomorphism from O/(pi^r) onto the kernel of O/(pi^(r+n+1)) -> O/(pi^(n+1)).
Surjectivity is the principal-ideal membership formula; injectivity cancels pi^(n+1)
in the domain O. The isomorphisms commute with the quotient reductions. Constant set sheafification preserves these pullback diagrams by left exactness. Its canonical comparison with underlying sets of constant ring sheaves transports the quotient maps and multiplication; naturality of the sheafification unit checks that comparison on constants. Evaluation computes the kernels sectionwise.
Apply the inverse isomorphisms to the shifted projections of x. Their compatibility
produces a section y of the original inverse-limit sheaf, using the sectionwise limit
universal property. Multiplying y by the constant pi^(n+1) has the same projection as x
at every level, hence equals x. For levels below n+1 use that both reduce to zero;
for higher levels use the defining finite-level isomorphism. The constant pi section
in the completion is the image under the actual constant-to-completed limit lift,
so the scalar used here is exactly the one displayed. This proves the claim for every
site object, with independent site and coefficient universes; no sheafification is
interchanged with an infinite limit.

proof_origin: Stage 3 complete Lean proof: finite multiplication pullbacks, left-exact set sheafification, compatible division, the sectionwise limit equivalence, and exact scalar normalization.

mathlib_searches.query: The kernel of the projection from a sheafwise completion over a discrete valuation ring to a finite quotient is the principal ideal generated by the uniformizer power
mathlib_searches.results: PadicInt.ker_toZModPow, AdicCompletion.kerProj, AdicCompletion.kerProj_of and PadicInt.ker_toZMod concern ring-level completions or p-adic integers, not the completed ring sheaf on arbitrary site objects. The project ConstantCompletion.flat_and_quotients gives the analogous formula on its same-universe small-site model; transporting the quotient and completion identifications to the present independent universes remains necessary.
AdicCompletion.evalₐ, surjective_evalₐ, ext_evalₐ, evalₐ_of, evalₐ_mk and factor_eval_eq_evalₐ are ring-completion evaluation lemmas; none states the sheafwise principal-kernel formula.

Mathlib hits primarily concern polynomial evaluation kernels. Reading Ideal/IsPrincipalPowQuotient.lean finds Ideal.quotEquivPowQuotPowSucc, a ring-module finite-level ingredient, not the sheafwise limit statement.

mathlib_searches.query: The kernel of a projection from the limit of constant uniformizer power quotient sheaves is divisible by the corresponding uniformizer power
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits, including LinearMap.IsProj.isCompl, LinearMap.ker_linearProjOfIsCompl, Submodule.ker_mkQ and CategoryTheory.Limits.instHasKernelπ. These concern module projections, quotient kernels or categorical biproducts, not uniformizer divisibility in a sheafwise completion; no exact match.

lean.statement:
theorem completedIntegralProjection_divisible
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (T : Scheme.{t})
    (n : ℕ) (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ)
    (x : (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E T).obj.obj U)
    (_hx : (limit.π (integralCoefficientSheafSystem l E T) (op n)).hom.app U x = 0) :
    ∃ y : (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E T).obj.obj U,
      x = ((integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l E T).hom.app U
        ((toSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
          ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
            (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{t + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))))).app U
              (ULift.up (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)))) ^ (n + 1) * y
